title: Priority Queue
solution: Compute the contribution of each +X operation separately. Force that operation into the chosen subsequence, then scan all operations with dp[position][smaller], where smaller counts selected active insertions ordered before X by (value, original index). Skipping an operation preserves the state; selecting a smaller insertion increments it; selecting a deletion decrements it when possible. After X has been inserted, transitions that would delete X from state zero are forbidden. Summing the final states gives the number of subsequences in which X survives, so multiplying by X and summing over insertions gives the answer in O(n^3) time and O(n^2) memory.

review.rationale: The official tutorial explicitly fixes each inserted value, counts subsequences in which it remains, and uses a DP over the number of smaller active values. contribution-technique and subsequence-dp describe the two essential ideas. The judge's ternary-search tag is not used by the editorial solution and is retained only as source metadata.

rejected_patterns.reason: A priority queue defines the simulated process, but no heap is used in the counting algorithm.
The official O(n^3) contribution DP performs no ternary search.
The state counts active values below a fixed pivot; it does not maintain weighted moments that close a polynomial transition.

taxonomy_decision.subsequence-dp: Canonicalized because it is a reusable include-or-skip DP family and was already present as an open-vocabulary label in the corpus.
taxonomy_decision.moment-dp: Added as a canonical DP subtype for transitions that close by tracking aggregate weighted moments. Expected Product 2 is a clear instance: its zeroth and first moments form a two-state linear recurrence.
